title: 4/05 1am check-results re-applied the scheduler's already-recorded 4/04 result: local streak 4 instead of 2
tier_reason: local state corruption: streak.json double-counted the 4/04 result, and streak.json was the MDP's streak input for the next decisions until corrected

contract.text: Each graded date changes the streak exactly once; the 1am check-results cron skips dates the scheduler has already resolved.
contract.source: ARCHITECTURE.md at 0e23c0f ('1am cron remains as a safety-net bts check-results fallback'); made explicit at bc520a7 ('Skips when scheduler has already set result ("hit"/"miss") to avoid double-counting streak')

mechanism.text: the scheduler's result polling resolved 4/04 mid-game and applied it to streak.json; the 1am check_results then re-graded the same date without checking daily.result and called update_streak a second time

residual.text: check-results, reconcile and the daemon's result polling remained independent, unlocked writers of pick files and streak.json until the July scoring-lock work (49f2538, 7/10: 'every result writer now locked and clobber-safe')

watchdog.trigger: after the nightly grading jobs, streak.json differs from a forward replay of the season's graded pick files (or from the contest's active streak when available)
watchdog.recovery_assertion: streak.json equals the replayed (and contest) streak before the next decision

evidence.what: the 1am check-results cron was double-counting the streak when the scheduler had already updated it mid-game; 'Bug caused streak to show 4 instead of correct 2 after April 4'

evidence.locator: src/bts/cli.py check_results and src/bts/scheduler.py run_result_polling at 4cf7b1e
evidence.what: both call update_streak on the same date; check_results had no already-resolved guard
each decision loads streak.json (load_streak) and passes it to select_pick, whose MDP action depends on the streak
